entities.summary:
Victor of Damask (b. 150 CE) was a public servant or civil administrator of the Classical era, an age of empires, philosophical inquiry, and foundational civilizations, active in the Roman Empire.

He served as a military leader and commander in various campaigns, including the Parthian War, contributing to the Roman Empire's expansion in the East.

Victor's administrative skills and strategic prowess earned him recognition among his peers, and he was eventually appointed as a high-ranking official in the Roman government.

His legacy can be seen in the continued Roman influence in the region, which lasted for centuries after his death in 177 CE.

In the words of the Roman historian Cassius Dio, 'Victor of Damask was a man of great courage and cunning, who served the Roman Empire with distinction.'
